transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood Product), Samantha Green (ACME Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (ACME Platform Eng), Rachel Kim (ACME PM)

Auto-generated summary (note: edits may be needed):
Redwood ran a demo of the Eval/Quality Monitoring workflow (Console + Optimize + API) focusing on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Customer is interested in automated regression detection tied to prompt sets and running A/Bs against current hosted model. Key asks: how to import existing prompt sets, how regression alerts surface, onboarding steps for POC, data residency and SSO. Next steps agreed: share eval workbook, provision trial, schedule POC kickoff.

Topics:
- Eval prompt sets (creation, tagging, pass/fail criteria)
- Regression alerts and baselines
- A/B comparison dashboards and rollouts
- Integration points: API, Console export, webhooks
- Security questions: SSO/SAML, audit logs, data retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya on the call for a demo of our eval and quality monitoring flows. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Samantha (ACME): Good, thanks. Excited to see how you handle regression alerts — we've had a bunch of silent failures recently.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah totally, that's what we'll focus on. We'll walk through prompt sets, how you define pass/fail, then show the automated regression alerts and an A/B comparison flow. I'll flip to the Console in a sec — please forgive any tiny UI name typos, sometimes the screen share labels come out as "Redwood Optmize" in my headset.
[00:32] Liam (ACME): Sounds good. We're especially interested in integrating with our CI and Slack alerts.
[00:36] Jordan: Great. Quick qualification — Samantha, Rachel, can you confirm the current stack? Are you using a hosted API (OpenAI) today or self-hosted models? And who owns the prompt sets?
[00:46] Samantha: We're mostly on a mix — internal hosted endpoints via OpenAI for prod, some on SageMaker-hosted models for edge dev. Prompt sets live in a Google Sheet maintained by the PMs, Rachel owns them.
[00:56] Rachel (ACME): Yep, that's us. We have about 1.2k prompts total, but only ~300 are used for evaluations right now. We have a few golden prompts and many failing edge cases.
[01:08] Priya: Perfect. I'll show how to import those prompt sets, tag them (e.g., intent, persona, failure-mode), and attach expected outputs or checks.
[01:17] [01:17] Priya (screen share): Ok, here's the Console. On the left nav you'll see "Optimize" -> "Evals" — sometimes the transcription calls it "Optmize Evals" but it's the same flow. We can import CSV/JSON or pull from your S3 bucket or Git repo.
[01:30] Samantha: Do you preserve prompt metadata? We need to keep prompt owner and last-updated.
[01:34] Priya: Yes, metadata fields are preserved on import and you can map extra columns. We also store a prompt id so you can do time-series comparisons.
[01:42] [01:42] Priya: Here's a sample eval set — notice columns: prompt_id, input, expected_output, tolerance (BLEU/ROUGE/str match), tags, owner. You can add structured checks (regex, semantic similarity threshold).
[01:55] Liam: How do you define pass/fail for non-deterministic models?
[01:58] Priya: Good q — we support multiple checkers: exact match (for deterministic responses), fuzzy text similarity, QA-style F1, and human labels if you want. You can also provide multiple expected outputs and configure scoring weights.
[02:12] Samantha: So the regression alert — does it trigger per-prompt or per-batch?
[02:16] Priya: Both. You can set alerts on per-prompt thresholds (e.g., prompt X drops below 0.7 similarity) and aggregate alerts across sets (e.g., >5% regression across the user-facing intent set). Alerts can be emailed, sent to Slack, or hit a webhook for your CI.
[02:33] [02:33] Priya: Let me trigger a simulated run against two model versions — current-hosted and Redwood-optimized.
[02:38] [02:38] (sound of typing)
[02:45] Priya: Running eval... this will take a minute. You can see in the UI we log per-prompt latencies, token costs (approx), and a diff view that highlights changed outputs. Note: cost estimates are based on token model types; if you use self-hosted models we estimate based on throughput and config.
[03:05] Samantha: Nice, is the KV cache considered in the latency measurement? We've got stateful prompts that use context windows.
[03:11] Priya: We surface cold vs warm latency. Cold includes model load and cold KV cache; warm measures steady-state with KV cache hits. Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching so you can see the delta.
[03:23] [03:23] Priya: Ok the run completed — you can see prompt-level pass rates and a regression heatmap. For this synthetic run, model v2 has a 4.8% regression on the payments intent set.
[03:35] Rachel: Can we dig into the specific failing prompts? I want to see diffs inline.
[03:39] Priya: Sure — clicking a failed prompt shows side-by-side responses with highlighted token diffs, similarity score, and a suggested remediation — often a prompt tweak or increasing re-rank beam.
[03:52] Miguel (Redwood Product): And we can auto-link failing prompts to your ticketing system. We have a built-in Zapier/webhook integration — or a native Jira connector if you prefer.
[04:03] Samantha: Security question — where do logs and eval outputs reside? We need SOC 2 logs and audit trail.
[04:09] Jordan: Good callout. For hosted customers we retain eval logs per your retention policy — configurable. For Dedicated/Private deployments logs can stay in your VPC or S3 and we support KMS keys. Audit logs and SSO/SAML are available. We'll share the security pack.
[04:24] Samantha: Do you support SAML assertions and SCIM for provisioning?
[04:28] Jordan: Yes — SSO via SAML, SCIM for user sync, RBAC at route/model level. We'll include the spec in the security docs.
[04:36] [04:36] Priya: Back to A/B flows — here's a quick demo of an A/B experiment. You create two routes: route A pointing at your current provider, route B pointing at Redwood-optimized model. You can run traffic split, tie the experiment to an eval set, and watch live metrics (pass rate, latency, cost).
[04:55] Liam: Does Redwood handle warm-ups so the latency is comparable between endpoints?
[04:59] Priya: Yes you can configure pre-warming and traffic ramp-up policies. The A/B runner can execute warmup calls before measuring.
[05:08] Samantha: What about model rollouts — can you do canary with automatic rollback on regressions?
[05:12] Priya: Absolutely. The rollout engine can auto-failover if regression thresholds are met; you can set thresholds on multiple metrics. And there's a manual override.
[05:22] Rachel: For our POC we want to run an A/B against a set of 500 prompts and have alerts for any prompt dropping below 0.7 similarity. Is that feasible?
[05:31] Priya: Totally feasible — you can import your 500 prompts or point to S3. We'll run the eval continuously or on schedule. For the POC we usually run nightly and set Slack alerts for first-failure and aggregate daily summaries.
[05:44] Jordan: Quick note on pricing — for eval runs we bill per eval token and a small orchestration fee for managed runs. I'll send a pricing sheet after.
[05:54] Samantha: Another compliance question — can we store only hashes of user-provided expected outputs to meet privacy constraints?
[05:59] Miguel: Yes, we support hashed expectations and PLAINTEXT redaction. Also Private deployment can keep all artifacts in your VPC. We'll include the technical notes.
[06:12] [06:12] (short silence)
[06:14] Priya: Alright, last piece — integrations. We have a REST API to kick off eval jobs, fetch results, and fetch per-prompt history. Webhooks for alerts, and the Console to explore results. Some customers do a hybrid: trigger evals from their CI and send diffs to Slack.
[06:30] Liam: For the API, do you have SDKs? We prefer Python and Go.
[06:34] Priya: Yes — we have official Python and Go SDKs plus a curl-based REST reference. We'll send example snippets.
[06:41] Samantha: Curious — can you do A/B at scale with low additional token cost? How do you avoid doubling inference costs for two endpoints?
[06:48] Priya: Two approaches: 1) Run sampling-based A/B where only a subset of traffic hits the B model, or 2) run offline evals using cached responses (replay) to avoid double real-time inference. Optimize has replay tooling to run huge evals efficiently.
[07:04] Rachel: For our team, we'd prefer scheduled offline eval runs nightly and real-time sampling for small percentages.
[07:09] Priya: Works well. We'll help set the thresholds.
[07:12] Samantha: Anything else we should know about regression alert tuning?
[07:15] Priya: Tuning calls for three things: pick stable metrics (semantic similarity often better than exact match), set rolling baselines (last 7 or 14 days), and use per-intent thresholds. We also support manual whitelists for known flakey prompts.
[07:30] Jordan: Ok let's recap and outline next steps.
[07:33] Jordan: Action items: we'll send the eval workbook and pricing, provision a trial, Priya will prepare a sample A/B dashboard and synthetic prompt set, Samantha will share their prompt sheet. We also flagged security docs to send. Any additions?
[07:46] Samantha: That covers it. Could you also include a short runbook for onboarding?
[07:50] Jordan: Yes we'll include a POC runbook.
[07:53] Rachel: Timeline — we aim to start the POC next week if we can get access.
[07:57] Jordan: We'll target week of 2025-02-17 for kickoff.
[08:00] (meeting wraps, brief chit-chat)
